mainTopic: The number and kind of distinctions in הבדלה, the מעין חתימה rule, and how the ברכה of הבדלה ends
overview: The גמרא explains why the Master's הבדלה, which listed four distinctions, does not break the rule of three to seven. The line 'between the seventh day and the six days of work' is not counted. It is a lead-in that matches the closing of the ברכה, following שמואל's rule. The scholars of פומבדיתא say instead to echo the opening of the ברכה, and the two versions differ when יום טוב falls right after שבת. The גמרא then examines רבי אושעיא's rule of no fewer than three and no more than seven. It answers a תוספתא that allows one distinction by calling it a dispute between תנאים, and it rules against the one-distinction view. רבי יהושע בן לוי adds that the distinctions must be ones the תורה calls a הבדלה. To fit his rule, 'sea and dry land' is struck from a ברייתא, and the count of seven is restored by splitting כהנים, לוים and ישראלים into two. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about how the ברכה ends. רב's 'מקדש ישראל' is sharply rejected, and a ברייתא praises combining both endings.

steps.title: Four distinctions is neither three nor seven
steps.stepSummary: The questioner points out that the Master's הבדלה listed four distinctions, which matches neither of the expected counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master did not say three, and he did not say seven!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the Master's הבדלה. He listed four distinctions, but the expected number was three or seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Master listed: holy and חול, light and darkness, ישראל and the nations, and the seventh day and the six working days. That makes four. Four does not match either standard count, so his practice seems to break the accepted pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master', a respectful way of addressing a scholar

phrases.english: But the Master did not say three
and he did not say seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הבדלה text the Master recited earlier in the sugya
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The expected count is three or seven. Four fits neither, so his text looks wrong.

steps.title: The fourth line is not counted as a separate distinction
steps.stepSummary: The Master answers that 'between the seventh day and the six days of work' is not an extra distinction. It is a line that matches the closing of the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In truth, 'between the seventh day and the six days of work' is something similar to the closing.
steps.whatsHappening: The Master defends his text. He explains that the fourth line is not really counted, so he did say three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה ends with 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול.' The line about the seventh day and the six working days says the same idea in other words. So it works as a lead-in to the closing line, not as a new item on the list. That leaves three real distinctions.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to the closing line of the ברכה

phrases.english: He said to him: In truth,
'between the seventh day and the six days of work'
is something similar to the closing
phrases.notes: So it is not counted as one of the distinctions

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: one item is not part of the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four lines count as separate distinctions
steps.terutzMaskana: Only three count. The fourth is a lead-in to the closing line.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: say something like the closing near the closing
steps.stepSummary: The answer is backed by שמואל's rule that the person reciting הבדלה must say something similar to the closing right before the closing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One who recites הבדלה must say something similar to the closing, near its closing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a rule from שמואל that explains why the Master added the fourth line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל requires a phrase that echoes the closing line, placed just before that closing. The 'seventh day and six working days' line does exactly this job. That is why it is required, and it also explains why it is not counted as a distinction.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who recites havdala must say
something similar to the closing, near its closing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the answer in step 2
steps.raayaObject: The fourth line has a special role and is not counted
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule of מעין חתימה סמוך לחתימתו
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle shapes how many ברכות are built: right before the closing 'ברוך אתה' line, we echo what the closing will say.

steps.title: פומבדיתא: echo the opening near the closing
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of פומבדיתא hold that the phrase before the closing should match the opening of the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the scholars of פומבדיתא say: something similar to their opening, near their closing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the rule. In this version, the phrase near the end should echo how the ברכה began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says to echo the closing line. פומבדיתא says to echo the opening line. Most of the time the opening and closing of a ברכה say the same thing, so it is not yet clear whether this changes anything. That sets up the next question.

phrases.english: And the scholars of Pumbedita say:
something similar to their opening, near their closing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of שמואל's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase before the closing should match the opening of the ברכה

steps.title: What difference is there between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two versions ever lead to a different practice. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the opening and closing of a ברכה match, so both rules would require the same words. The גמרא wants a case where they split apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two versions in steps 3 and 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'echo the closing' and 'echo the opening' lead to different wording

steps.title: The case: יום טוב right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת. In that case the ברכה closes with 'בין קודש לקודש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a יום טוב that falls after שבת, when we close with 'between holy and holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case where the two versions split: הבדלה said on a יום טוב night that comes right after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the ברכה opens with 'between holy and חול,' but it closes with 'between holy and holy.' Now the opening and the closing are different. So 'echo the opening' and 'echo the closing' point to different wording.

keyTerms.term: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: a יום טוב that falls right after שבת
between holy and holy (the closing for שבת going into יום טוב)

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: a Festival that falls after Shabbat,
when we close with 'between holy and holy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 5 by naming the case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום טוב on מוצאי שבת, where the opening and the closing of the ברכה differ

steps.title: How each version handles that case
steps.stepSummary: Under the 'echo the opening' version, there is no need to say 'between the holiness of שבת and the holiness of יום טוב.' Under the 'echo the closing' version, that line is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says to echo the opening near the closing, one need not say 'between the holiness of שבת and the holiness of יום טוב You have distinguished.' According to the one who says to echo the closing near the closing, one must say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how each version changes the wording on that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening is about holy and חול, so the 'echo the opening' version has nothing new to add. The closing is about holy and holy, so the 'echo the closing' version (שמואל's) needs a lead-in line about שבת's holiness versus יום טוב's holiness.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions only split when the opening and the closing of the ברכה differ, as on יום טוב after שבת. שמואל's version requires the extra line 'בין קדושת שבת לקדושת יום טוב הבדלת.'

phrases.english: The one who says
something similar to their opening, near their closing,
does not require saying:

phrases.aramaic: ״בֵּין קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב הִבְדַּלְתָּ״.
phrases.english: 'Between the holiness of Shabbat and the holiness of the Festival You have distinguished.'
And the one who says
something similar to their closing, near their closing,
requires saying:

phrases.aramaic: ״בֵּין קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב הִבְדַּלְתָּ״.
phrases.english: 'Between the holiness of Shabbat and the holiness of the Festival You have distinguished.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵעֵין פְּתִיחָתָן סָמוּךְ לַחֲתִימָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'echo the closing' version requires the line 'בין קדושת שבת לקדושת יום טוב הבדלת.' The 'echo the opening' version does not.

steps.title: Back to the source: no fewer than three, no more than seven
steps.stepSummary: With the word גופא, the גמרא returns to examine רבי אלעזר's statement in the name of רבי אושעיא about how many distinctions to mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: One who mentions fewer should not mention fewer than three, and one who mentions more should not mention more than seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the statement it quoted earlier so it can study it on its own. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of distinctions in הבדלה has a range. The minimum is three and the maximum is seven. The challenge in step 1 was built on this statement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself', the formula for returning to analyze a statement quoted earlier

steps.confusionAlert: גופא does not introduce a new teacher's opinion. It brings back a statement already quoted so the גמרא can now examine it in detail.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
One who mentions fewer should not mention fewer than three,
and one who mentions more should not mention more than seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the closing line and returns to the base statement on how many distinctions to mention
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הבדלה should mention at least three distinctions and at most seven

steps.title: A teaching that says one distinction is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא with a תוספתא. It says a person who is not used to it may say just one distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: One says distinctions at the end of שבת, at the end of יום טוב, and at the end of יום כיפור. One also says them when שבת ends into יום טוב, and when יום טוב ends into חול המועד. But one does not say them when יום טוב ends into שבת. Someone who is used to it says many distinctions. Someone who is not used to it says one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a תוספתא to attack the rule from Step 8 that a person must say at least three distinctions. The last line of the תוספתא says one distinction is enough for someone who is not used to saying more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא set a minimum of three distinctions. This source allows a person to say only one. That means three is not required, which goes against רבי אושעיא's minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected: the גמרא brings a source to challenge a statement
The middle days of a festival
Someone who is used to it

steps.confusionAlert: When יום טוב ends and שבת begins, we do not say הבדלה distinctions. We are moving up to a holier day, not down to a less holy one.

phrases.english: They objected:
One says distinctions at the end of Shabbatot
and at the end of Festivals
and at the end of Yom Kippur,
and at the end of Shabbat going into a Festival

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב לְחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: and at the end of a Festival going into the intermediate days,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but not at the end of a Festival going into Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Shabbat is holier than a Festival, so this is not a step down.

phrases.english: One who is used to it says many,
and one who is not used to it says one.
phrases.notes: This is the line that makes the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's minimum of three distinctions from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא: one may not say fewer than three distinctions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא allows a single distinction, so three cannot be the minimum.

steps.title: This is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים argued about this. One view says one distinction, and common practice is three.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As רבי יוחנן said: The son of holy ones says one distinction, but the people were used to saying three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that תנאים argued about this question. רבי אושעיא simply follows the view that requires three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תוספתא is not a final ruling. It reflects one side of an argument. רבי יוחנן reports that one great sage said one distinction, while the people's custom was three, which supports רבי אושעיא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The son of holy ones, a title of honor

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
the son of holy ones says one,
and the people were accustomed to say three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between Tannaim: the challenging source reflects only one view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תוספתא proves that three distinctions are not required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other תנאים and common practice require three, which supports רבי אושעיא.

steps.title: Who is the son of holy ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'son of holy ones' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'the son of holy ones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask who this honored person is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question to identify the speaker. It does not change the הלכה being discussed.

phrases.english: Who is 'the son of holy ones'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the sage named in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of 'the son of holy ones'

steps.title: He is רבי מנחם בר סימאי
steps.stepSummary: The 'son of holy ones' is רבי מנחם בר סימאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מנחם בר סימאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'son of holy ones' is רבי מנחם בר סימאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know which sage held that one distinction is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage called 'the son of holy ones'

phrases.english: Rabbi Menaḥem bar Simai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'son of holy ones' is רבי מנחם בר סימאי.

steps.title: Why he was given that title
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he was called 'son of holy ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call him 'the son of holy ones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what earned him this special title.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another short side question about the sage, not about הבדלה.

phrases.english: And why did they call him 'the son of holy ones'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the identity given in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the title 'son of holy ones'

steps.title: He never looked at images on coins
steps.stepSummary: He would not even look at the images on coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he did not look at the image on a coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that he earned the title because he never looked at the images stamped on coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins sometimes had idolatrous or forbidden images. Avoiding even a glance at them showed unusual holiness.

phrases.english: Because he did not look at the image on a coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He never looked at the forms engraved on coins.

steps.title: Another sage also said one distinction
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אידי reported that his brother חנניא also said only one distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אידי sent to him: My brother חנניא says one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a report that another sage, חנניא, also held that one distinction is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבי מנחם בר סימאי was not alone in holding the one-distinction view. It sets up the final ruling in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Idi sent to him:
Ḥananya my brother says one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporter of the one-distinction view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניא also holds that one distinction is enough.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow the one-distinction view
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is not like the view that one distinction is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that we do not follow the view that one distinction is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical ruling stays with רבי אושעיא and the people's custom. One should say at least three distinctions.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is to say at least three distinctions in הבדלה, as the people's custom was. The view of one distinction is rejected.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the dispute from Steps 10 and 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not rule that one distinction is enough. The minimum of three stands.

steps.title: Distinctions must match those in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the distinctions said in הבדלה must be ones the תורה calls a 'הבדלה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who makes הבדלה must say distinctions like the ones stated in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins about which distinctions you may say. רבי יהושע בן לוי says they must be like distinctions the תורה itself mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from how many distinctions to which ones. Only pairs that the תורה describes using the language of separating (הבדלה) qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the style of
That are stated in the תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
one who makes havdala must say
distinctions like those stated in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which distinctions may be said, rather than how many.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only distinctions that the תורה describes with the language of הבדלה may be said.

steps.title: A ברייתא with a long list of distinctions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists the order of distinctions and the possible endings for the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: What is the order of distinctions? One says: 'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, and between the seventh day and the six working days, between impure and pure, between the sea and dry land, between the upper waters and the lower waters, between כהנים, לויים and ישראלים.' One closes with 'the order of creation.' Others say: with 'Who forms creation.' רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: one closes with 'Who sanctifies Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יהושע בן לוי. This step quotes the source. The actual problem is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists eight pairs, starting with 'between holy and ordinary.' The 'seventh day' line is only a lead-in to the closing and is not counted, so the list counts as seven distinctions. The ברייתא also gives three opinions on how to close the ברכה. One item on the list, 'between the sea and dry land,' is about to cause a problem.

phrases.english: They objected:
What is the order of distinctions?
One says: 'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary,
between light and darkness,
between Israel and the nations,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: and between the seventh day and the six days of work,
between impure and pure,
between the sea and the dry land,
phrases.notes: This is the item the challenge will focus on.

phrases.english: between the upper waters and the lower waters,
between priests, Levites, and Israelites.'
And he closes with 'the order of creation.'
And others say: with 'Who forms creation.'
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
he closes with 'Who sanctifies Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that will be used to challenge Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that distinctions must be ones stated in the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's list includes an item that may not be a תורה-stated הבדלה. The problem is spelled out in Step 19.

steps.title: Sea and dry land is not called a הבדלה in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהושע בן לוי is right, the ברייתא should not include 'between the sea and dry land,' because the תורה never uses the word הבדלה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, 'between the sea and the dry land' does not have the word 'separation' written about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the challenge clearly. 'Between the sea and dry land' is on the ברייתא's list, but the תורה does not call it a הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the creation story, the תורה uses the word for separating about light and dark and about the upper and lower waters. It does not use it for the sea and dry land. So the ברייתא seems to allow a distinction that רבי יהושע בן לוי would not allow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not written about it

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the sea and dry land were never separated. The problem is only that the תורה does not use the word 'הבדלה' for it.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
behold, 'between the sea and the dry land'
does not have 'separation' written about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the attack hidden in the ברייתא of Step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes a distinction that the תורה never calls a הבדלה. That contradicts the rule that only תורה-stated distinctions may be said.

steps.title: Remove sea and dry land from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by striking 'between the sea and dry land' from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove from here 'between the sea and the dry land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by fixing the ברייתא's text. It removes the line about the sea and dry land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting רבי יהושע בן לוי, the גמרא edits the ברייתא. Once that line is gone, every distinction left on the list fits his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from here: delete this from the text

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule stands: the distinctions in הבדלה must be ones the תורה calls a 'הבדלה.' The line 'between the sea and dry land' is taken out of the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא is willing to correct the text of a ברייתא to keep an accepted rule intact. This explains why our הבדלה uses only distinctions that the תורה itself describes as separations.

phrases.english: Remove from here 'between the sea and the dry land.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: deleting a phrase from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows a distinction that the תורה does not call a הבדלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: That line does not belong in the ברייתא, so the ברייתא fully fits רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Now the list is short of seven
steps.stepSummary: With 'sea and dry land' removed, and 'the seventh day and the six days of work' not counting either, the list has only six distinctions.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'between the seventh day and the six days of work' should also not count, because it is only said as a lead-in to the ending. That means one is missing, and there are not seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a new problem caused by the last answer: after removing 'sea and dry land,' the list no longer reaches seven distinctions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 2) the גמרא said that the 'seventh day' line is a מעין חתימה (a lead-in that matches the ending), so it does not count as a distinction. The ברייתא's long version is supposed to reach the maximum of seven that רבי אושעיא allows. Once 'sea and dry land' is taken out and the 'seventh day' line is not counted, only six real distinctions remain: holy and ordinary, light and darkness, ישראל and the nations, impure and pure, upper and lower waters, and כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if we accept what was just said
A line that matches the ending of the ברכה, said just before it

steps.confusionAlert: The 'seventh day' line really is said in הבדלה. The question is only whether it counts toward the seven. Because it is a lead-in to the ending, it does not.

phrases.english: If so

phrases.aramaic: ״בֵּין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה״ נָמֵי?
phrases.english: 'between the seventh day and the six days of work' should also not count?
phrases.notes: This is a real item in the הבדלה text.

phrases.english: It is only a lead-in that matches the ending,
so one is missing, and there are not seven!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי ״בֵּין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה״ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks a side effect of the answer in Step 20, which struck 'sea and dry land.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of seven distinctions in the ברייתא after the correction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing one item and not counting the lead-in line leaves only six real distinctions.

steps.title: Priests, Levites and Israelites count as two distinctions
steps.stepSummary: The distinction between כהנים, לוים and ישראלים is really two distinctions, and each one has its own פסוק using the language of separating.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: 'כהנים, לוים and ישראלים' is two matters. Between לוים and ישראלים, as it is written: 'At that time ה׳ separated the tribe of לוי.' Between the כהנים and the לוים, as it is written: 'The sons of עמרם: אהרן and משה; and אהרן was separated to be sanctified as most holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the counting problem by showing that one line in the list really holds two distinctions, which brings the total back to seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate splits: ישראל from לוי, and כהן from לוי. Each one has a פסוק that uses a form of the word הבדלה (הִבְדִּיל, וַיִּבָּדֵל). So both also pass רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that every distinction must be one the תורה calls a 'הבדלה.'

keyTerms.meaning: They are two matters (two separate items)

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer keeps the count at seven and also fits רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule, because each distinction is backed by the actual word for 'separating' in a פסוק.

phrases.english: They answer: priests, Levites and Israelites
are two matters.
Between Levites and Israelites, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״בָּעֵת הַהִיא הִבְדִּיל ה׳ אֶת שֵׁבֶט הַלֵּוִי״.
phrases.english: 'At that time ה׳ separated the tribe of Levi.'
Between the priests and the Levites, as it is written:
'The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses;
and Aaron was separated to be sanctified as most holy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים תְּרֵי מִילֵּי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem raised in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting: one listed item is split into two distinctions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed כהנים, לוים and ישראלים is only one distinction, which left six.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is two distinctions, each backed by a פסוק that uses הבדלה language, so the total is seven.

steps.title: How does the ברכה of הבדלה end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what words should close the ברכה of הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he say at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the exact closing words of the ברכה. It is setting up the argument between רב and שמואל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every long ברכה ends with a short closing line, the חתימה, that begins with 'ברוך אתה ה׳'. The question is which idea the closing line of הבדלה should express.

phrases.english: When closing, what does he close with?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the middle of the ברכה (the list of distinctions) to how the ברכה ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct closing words of the הבדלה ברכה

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about the ending
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ending is 'מקדש ישראל'. שמואל says it is 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: 'Who sanctifies Israel.' And שמואל said: 'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to the question of how the ברכה ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ending focuses on Israel's holiness. שמואל's ending matches the main theme of הבדלה, which is separating. The two are arguing about which idea should seal the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary

phrases.english: Rav said: 'Who sanctifies Israel,'
and Shmuel said:
'Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 23 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: 'מקדש ישראל'. שמואל: 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול'.

steps.title: אביי strongly rejects רב's ending
steps.stepSummary: אביי (some say רב יוסף) cursed, meaning sharply objected to, ending הבדלה like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, and some say רב יוסף, cursed this view of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that a later אמורא strongly rejected רב's ending for הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ending with 'מקדש ישראל' does not match what הבדלה is about, which is separating. So the sharp reaction against רב leans toward שמואל's ending. The word 'cursed' shows how strongly he disapproved; it does not mean an actual curse on רב himself.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)

steps.confusionAlert: The disapproval is aimed at following רב's ending for הבדלה. It is not a personal attack on רב.

phrases.english: Abaye cursed it,
and some say it was Rav Yosef,
regarding this view of Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָיֵיט עֲלַהּ אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף אַהָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts against רב's opinion from Step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It does not fit a ברכה whose whole theme is separating.

steps.title: A blessing for one who ends with both phrases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהושע בן חנניה says that someone who ends with both 'מקדש ישראל' and 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' will have his days and years lengthened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן חנניה: Anyone who ends with 'Who sanctifies Israel and distinguishes between holy and ordinary' will have his days and years lengthened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that praises an ending which combines both phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a third option: joining רב's phrase and שמואל's phrase into one ending. The ברייתא gives no legal proof. It promises a reward of long life to someone who ends this way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the name of
His days and years are lengthened

steps.whatToRemember: The middle of הבדלה mentions seven distinctions, and כהנים, לוים and ישראלים count as two. For the ending, רב says 'מקדש ישראל' and שמואל says 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול'. רב's ending is sharply rejected, and a ברייתא praises combining both phrases. Our normal practice on מוצאי שבת is to end like שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
Anyone who ends with 'Who sanctifies Israel
and distinguishes between holy and ordinary,'
his days and years are lengthened.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a combined ending alongside the two opinions of רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ending with both 'מקדש ישראל' and 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' earns long life.
